name: Lamu Old Town
description: The UNESCO-listed core of coral-stone houses, carved doors, and narrow winding lanes travelled on foot and by donkey. The seafront and bustling market are here, along with mosques, guesthouses, and the everyday life of the island. Atmospheric, historic, and endlessly walkable.
bestFor: Culture seekers and first-time visitors wanting the real Swahili town
pros: Central to markets, boats, and daily life
cons: Busy, dense, and can feel rough-edged

name: Shela
tagline: The beach village with the long dune
description: A quieter, prettier village a short walk or boat ride from Lamu town, backed by a long dune-fringed beach. Home to boutique hotels, expat-owned houses, and relaxed seafront restaurants, Shela is the polished, laid-back side of the island and the favourite base for many longer-stay visitors.
bestFor: Slow-travel nomads wanting comfort, beach access, and calm
pros: Long, beautiful beach on the doorstep
Calmer and quieter than the old town

name: Manda Island
tagline: Across the channel by the airstrip
description: The island facing Lamu across the channel, home to the Manda airstrip where flights from Nairobi and Mombasa land. Quieter and more spread out, it holds a few resorts, ruins, and secluded spots, and every arrival passes through here before a short boat transfer to Lamu or Shela.
bestFor: Travellers wanting seclusion or easy airstrip access
pros: Home to the airstrip and main arrival point
cons: Separated from town life by water

name: Langoni and Mkomani
description: The residential quarters of Lamu Old Town, Langoni toward the south and Mkomani toward the north, away from the busiest seafront and market. These lanes offer a calmer, more local feel while keeping you within the historic town, with guesthouses and family homes tucked among the coral-stone streets.
bestFor: Visitors wanting old-town charm with less bustle
pros: Still walkable to markets and boats
